items.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL.
METHODS: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria.
RESULTS: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

items.title: HB0025 With Chemotherapy for Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Phase 2 Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Bispecific antibodies targeting vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)/PD-1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) pathways represent a promising therapeutic strategy for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). HB0025 is a novel bispecific antibody fusion targeting PD-L1 and VEGF.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of HB0025 plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced, driver variant-negative NSCLC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, multicenter, phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial enrolled patients with stage IIIB/C or IV NSCLC without sensitizing EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alterations across 13 hospitals in China. Participants included those with nonsquamous NSCLC and squamous NSCLC. Patients were enrolled from January 15, 2024, to May 21, 2025. Data cutoff was April 20, 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients received intravenous 10-mg/kg HB0025 every 3 weeks or 20-mg/kg HB0025 every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy: pemetrexed/carboplatin for nonsquamous and paclitaxel/carboplatin for squamous for up to 6 cycles, followed by HB0025 maintenance (with pemetrexed for nonsquamous) until disease progression or unacceptable toxic effects.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end points were safety and investigator-assessed objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors, version 1.1. The secondary end points included disease control rate, duration of response, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS).
RESULTS: Treatment efficacy was evaluable in 169 enrolled patients. The nonsquamous cohort included 85 patients (median [IQR] age, 63.0 [58.0-68.0] years; 26 [30.6%] female and 59 [69.4%] male patients), and the squamous cohort included 84 patients (median [IQR] age, 65.0 [60.0-69.0] years; 6 [7.1%] female and 78 [92.9%] male patients). In the nonsquamous cohort, confirmed ORR was 36.4% (95% CI, 17.2%-59.3%) and 57.1% (95% CI, 44.1%-69.5%) in the 10-mg/kg and 20-mg/kg dose groups, respectively. In the squamous cohort, ORR reached 68.2% (95% CI, 45.1%-86.1%) and 74.2% (95%, 61.5%-84.5%) at the respective doses. Median PFS was 12.52 months (95% CI, 10.15-16.56) in the nonsquamous cohort and 14.78 months (95% CI, 11.30 to not estimable) in the squamous cohort. The 12-month PFS rates were 54.3% (95% CI, 41.6%-65.3%) and 62.1% (95% CI, 49.9%-72.1%) in the nonsquamous and squamous cohorts, and the 12-month OS rates were 75.8% (95% CI, 65.0%-83.7%) and 85.5% (95% CI, 75.8%-91.5%) , respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 56 of 85 patients (65.9%) in the nonsquamous cohort and 51 of 84 (60.7%) in the squamous cohort, mainly as hematologic toxic effects. Any-grade immune-related adverse events related to HB0025 occurred in 20 patients (23.5%) in the nonsquamous cohort and 21 patients (25%) in the squamous cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: In this phase 2 nonrandomized clinical trial, HB0025 plus chemotherapy showed promising antitumor activity and manageable safety in patients with advanced, driver variant-negative NSCLC in both nonsquamous and squamous histologic types, supporting further evaluation in randomized phase 3 clinical trials.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06758557.

items.title: Targeted Use of Computed Tomographic Coronary Angiography in Acute Chest Pain.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction has been ruled out in the emergency department remain at risk for cardiovascular events. Whether further investigation reduces this risk is unknown.
METHODS: In a multicenter, randomized, controlled trial, patients who presented to an emergency department in 14 hospitals across the United Kingdom were enrolled if myocardial infarction had been ruled out and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin testing indicated an intermediate risk of a cardiovascular event (maximum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I or T concentration, >5 ng per liter). Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either outpatient computed tomographic (CT) coronary angiography-guided care or standard care. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause.
RESULTS: From September 18, 2019, to May 11, 2023, a total of 3170 participants (median age, 61 years; female sex, 30.2%) were assigned to undergo CT coronary angiography (1587 participants) or receive standard care (1583 participants). At 90 days after randomization, CT coronary angiography had been performed in 1462 participants (92.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 35 participants (2.2%) in the standard-care group. Overall, 7 participants (0.4%) had a CT coronary angiography-related adverse event. After a median of 3.0 years, at which point the number of primary-outcome events in the standard-care group exceeded the prespecified minimum of 97, a primary-outcome event had occurred in 112 participants (7.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 116 (7.3%) in the standard-care group (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% confidence interval, 0.73 to 1.23; P = 0.71).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction had been ruled out, routine CT coronary angiography-guided management did not result in a lower incidence of subsequent myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; TARGET-CTCA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03952351.).

items.title: Activity and safety of first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel in triple-negative breast cancer: a single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pumitamig, an investigational bispecific antibody targeting programmed death ligand-1 and vascular endothelial growth factor A, has shown preliminary efficacy across several tumour types. We aimed to evaluate the safety and activity of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel as first-line treatment in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer.
METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 1b/2 trial conducted at ten sites (hospitals and cancer centres) in China, patients aged 18-75 years with histologically documented, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and one or more measurable lesion (as per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours, version 1.1) received first-line pumitamig (20 mg/kg intravenously once every 2 weeks) plus nab-paclitaxel (100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. In phase 1b, six patients received pumitamig (20 mg/kg once every 2 weeks intravenously plus nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle) and were monitored for treatment-emergent adverse events, before subsequent enrolment in phase 2. The primary endpoints were confirmed objective response rate and safety, assessed in the efficacy-evaluable population, defined as all patients who received one or more doses of study drug and had measurable disease at baseline and at least one efficacy assessment. This trial is registered with chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2200060400) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05918133), and is closed to recruitment.
FINDINGS: Between June 27, 2022, and March 15, 2023, 42 patients were enrolled, received one or more doses of pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel (median duration of exposure 9·0 months, 95% CI 6·9-11·7) and had one or more tumour assessments. All patients were Chinese and female; median age was 53 years (IQR 41-60). At a median follow-up of 35·2 months (95% CI 33·0-36·1), the confirmed objective response rate was 73·8% (95% CI 58·0-86·1; 31 of 42 patients), including one complete response and 30 partial responses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were decreased neutrophil count (13 [31%] of 42 patients), decreased white blood cell count (11 [26%]), proteinuria (six [14%]), and febrile neutropenia (five [12%]). Nine (21%) patients reported 14 treatment-related serious adverse events (alanine aminotransferase increased n=2; febrile neutropenia n=2; pancreatitis n=2; and ascites, aspartate aminotransferase increased, abdominal distension, γ-glutamyltransferase increased, blood alkaline phosphatase increased, cataract, macular oedema, and retinal vein occlusion all n=1). Treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation of both nab-paclitaxel and pumitamig in four (10%) patients, discontinuation of nab-paclitaxel only in three (7%) patients, and discontinuation of pumitamig only in two (5%) patients. There were no treatment-related deaths.
INTERPRETATION: Treatment with first-line pumitamig plus nab-paclitaxel showed encouraging antitumour activity in patients with advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer and a safety profile consistent with the mode of actions of both agents. These findings warrant further clinical evaluation in global phase 2 and 3 trials.
FUNDING: Biotheus (BioNTech group).

items.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.
METHODS: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.
RESULTS: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

items.title: Retatrutide, a Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist, for Treatment of Obesity.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retatrutide is a triple-receptor agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptors.
METHODS: In this phase 3, randomized, double-blind trial, we assigned adults with obesity without diabetes to receive a once-weekly subcutaneous injection of retatrutide (at a dose of 4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg) or placebo for 80 weeks. Primary outcomes (evaluated in the 9-mg and 12-mg groups each vs. placebo) were the percent change in body weight and the change in the WOMAC pain score (ranging from 1 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) in the subgroup of 574 participants with knee osteoarthritis and the change in the apnea-hypopnea index in the 243 participants with obstructive sleep apnea. For weight-related end points, intercurrent events were handled by a treatment-regimen estimand (intention-to-treat [ITT]). For end points in participants with knee osteoarthritis or obstructive sleep apnea, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure; ITT results are also reported.
RESULTS: A total of 2339 participants underwent randomization. The mean percent change in body weight in the retatrutide groups was -17.6% (4-mg dose), -23.7% (9-mg dose), and -25.0% (12-mg dose) versus -3.9% in the placebo group (differences, -19.8 and -21.0 percentage points, respectively; P<0.001 for both comparisons). Among the participants with knee osteoarthritis, the corresponding changes in the pain score in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid estimand were -3.2, -3.5, and -3.6 versus -1.9 with placebo (differences, -1.6 and -1.8 points; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -3.4, -3.9, and -4.1 versus -2.5 with placebo (differences, -1.4 and -1.6 points; both P<0.001). Among the participants with obstructive sleep apnea, the corresponding changes in events per hour in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid-treatment estimand were -22.9, -34.3, and -31.7 versus -9.9 (differences, -24.4 and -21.9; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -22.8, -34.3, and -32.1 versus -9.6 (differences, -24.7 and -22.5; both P<0.001). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with obesity, retatrutide resulted in significant weight reduction, reduced pain in participants with knee osteoarthritis, and reduced apnea-hypopnea events in participants with obstructive sleep apnea. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05929066.).

items.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial.
items.abstract: Resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) carries a high risk of postoperative recurrence, underscoring the need for effective perioperative therapies. This nonrandomized, noncomparative phase 2 trial evaluated neoadjuvant ivonescimab monotherapy (cohort 1) or in combination with chemotherapy (cohort 2), followed by surgery and adjuvant ivonescimab. In cohort 2, the major pathological response (MPR) rate was 70.1% (47/67; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 57.7-80.7); the lower bound of the 80% two-sided CI exceeded the historical control rate of 41% and the primary endpoint was met. The MPR rate in cohort 1 was 60.0% (6/10; 95% CI = 26.2-87.8). Among patients who achieved MPR, 83.3% (5/6) in cohort 1 and 97.9% (46/47) in cohort 2 had residual viable tumor (RVT) of ≤5%, respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 36.4% (4/11) patients in cohort 1 and 30.4% (24/79) of those in cohort 2, with no grade 3 or higher hemorrhage or treatment-related death. Treatment-related surgery delay occurred in one (1.3%) patient. Surgery-related AEs related to ivonescimab occurred in 10.0% (1/10) and 10.4% (7/67) patients in the two cohorts, respectively, with no grade 3 or higher events reported. These data support perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy as a promising strategy for resectable NSCLC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05247684 .

items.title: Thoracic epidural versus paravertebral blockade for reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain (TOPIC-2): open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness of paravertebral blockade versus thoracic epidural during the perioperative period in reducing chronic post-thoracotomy pain.
DESIGN: Open label, parallel group, superiority, multicentre, randomised controlled trial.
SETTING: 15 thoracic centres in the UK.
PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing thoracotomy randomised (1:1) to either paravertebral blockade or thoracic epidural using a web based service between January 2019 and September 2023.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants in the paravertebral group received three single-shot paravertebral injections of local anaesthetic before incision followed by placement of a paravertebral catheter. Participants in the epidural group had a thoracic epidural catheter placed and loaded with local anaesthetic before incision.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was incidence of chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six months after randomisation, defined as a 100 mm visual analogue score greater than or equal to 40 mm (indicating moderate pain) when considering worst chest pain over the past week. Secondary outcomes included acute pain (visual analogue score of 100 mm) and complications.
RESULTS: 770 patients were enrolled, of which 428 (56%) were male (mean (standard deviation, SD) age 66.6 (11.0) years). After 33 exclusions of patients after randomisation who did not proceed to thoracotomy, 737 remained in the modified intention-to-treat population (364 in the paravertebral group, 373 in the epidural group). Six months after randomisation, 59 (22%) of 272 participants in the paravertebral group and 47 (16%) of 292 participants in the epidural group developed chronic post-thoracotomy pain (adjusted risk ratio 1.32 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93 to 1.86), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI -0.01 to 0.11), P=0.12). During the acute phase, worst and average pain was greater on day 1 with paravertebral blockade (adjusted mean difference 7.7 mm (95% CI 2.8 to 12.5 mm) and 7.0 mm (95% CI 2.7 to 11.2 mm), respectively), but no different on days 2-3. Hypotension was less common in the paravertebral group than the epidural group (12% v 18%, respectively, adjusted risk ratio 0.66 (95% CI 0.46 to 0.94), adjusted risk difference -0.06 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.01)), as was pruritis (4% v 12%, adjusted risk ratio 0.37 (95% CI 0.21 to 0.64), adjusted risk difference -0.07 (95% CI -0.11 to -0.03)), although more participants in this group experienced urinary retention (12% v 6%, adjusted risk ratio 2.21 (95% CI 1.35 to 3.61), adjusted risk difference 0.05 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.09)), complications were similar otherwise.
CONCLUSIONS: Paravertebral blockade did not reduce chronic post-thoracotomy pain at six month follow-up compared to thoracic epidural. Thoracic epidural provided marginally better acute pain relief one day after the operation, but showed no difference thereafter. Postoperative complications were comparable between groups. The findings support the ongoing use of both techniques.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03677856.

items.title: Opposing microbiome-mediated axes link modifiable lifestyles to health and chronic diseases.
items.abstract: Analyses disentangling the role of the gut microbiome in linking lifestyle factors to health outcomes remain limited. Here, using fecal shotgun metagenomics from 6,803 adults in the Japanese 4D cohort, we identified two opposing microbiome-mediated axes linking lifestyle to health and 15 diseases. A health-associated axis enriched in microbial metabolism of dietary components was linked to plant-based, soy and dairy intake. In contrast, a disease-associated axis, enriched in oral-derived bacteria and pathobionts, was linked to refined carbohydrates and sedentary behavior. Starter culture microorganisms used to ferment foods did not show statistically significant mediation of the observed health effects. Alcohol was associated with both health- and disease-oriented mediation patterns involving microbial host-glycan utilization. Microbiome-defined health- and disease-oriented mediator axes were supported by fecal short-chain fatty acids and plasma cytokines from >1,700 individuals, revealing butyrate-associated anti-inflammatory and pro-inflammatory host profiles, respectively. Microbiome-based prediction (MADE) scores captured lifestyle-microbiome-disease mediation patterns and distinguished individual diseases across 13 independent external cohorts from the United States, China, Sweden, Russia and Australia. We identify the gut microbiome as a key mediator linking lifestyle to health and disease, providing a framework for microbiome-based assessment to guide lifestyle interventions for health promotion and disease prevention.

items.title: Evolving First-Line Treatment Strategies in ERBB2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Review.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The treatment landscape of ERBB2 (formerly HER2)-positive metastatic breast cancer has evolved substantially during the past decade, with emerging therapies challenging the long-standing induction-maintenance paradigm established by the CLEOPATRA trial (NCT00567190). However, optimal treatment selection, sequencing, and duration remain uncertain, particularly in the context of increasing therapeutic complexity and biologic heterogeneity.
OBSERVATIONS: Taxane-based chemotherapy combined with trastuzumab and pertuzumab has long been the standard first-line induction regimen, followed by maintenance anti-ERBB2 therapy with or without endocrine therapy based on hormone receptor status. Recent data from the DESTINY-Breast09 trial (DB09; NCT04784715) demonstrate superior progression-free survival with trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab, supporting its recent US Food and Drug Administration approval and prompting questions regarding the necessity of chemotherapy, optimal duration of antibody-drug conjugate therapy, and the role of a dual ERBB2 blockade. Maintenance strategies have also expanded, particularly in hormone receptor-positive disease, with incorporation of endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors, as demonstrated in the PATINA trial (NCT02947685). The HER2CLIMB-05 trial (NCT05132582) provided an additional maintenance approach using a triplet anti-ERBB2 strategy. These nonchemotherapy maintenance options are designed to have fewer toxic effects and better quality of life than chemotherapy-based strategies. These developments raise questions regarding the necessity of chemotherapy, optimal duration of antibody-drug conjugate therapy, and the role of dual ERBB2 blockade. Emerging biomarker-driven approaches, including the HER2DX assay and circulating tumor DNA, remain investigational and are not yet part of routine clinical practice but aim to optimize treatment selection. Novel strategies, such as chemotherapy-free regimens and sequential multiagent approaches, as in the SAPPHO study (NCT06439693), are challenging traditional paradigms.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The management of ERBB2-positive metastatic breast cancer is transitioning toward a more individualized approach that balances efficacy, toxic effects, and patient preferences. Integrating biomarker-driven strategies will be essential to optimize treatment selection, duration, and sequencing, with the goal of improving long-term outcomes while preserving quality of life.

items.title: Combining quizartinib with intensive chemotherapy for older patients with newly diagnosed AML: results of the UK NCRI AML18 trial.
items.abstract: We assessed the addition of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor quizartinib, following intensive chemotherapy and as maintenance, for patients aged >60 years with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) or high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome, regardless of FLT3 mutation status. Four hundred sixty three patients (median age, 68 years) were randomized (1:1) to receive quizartinib 40 mg or not for 14 days immediately following chemotherapy courses 2 and 3, plus 28 additional days; those allocated quizartinib were further randomized (1:1) to either 12 additional 28-day maintenance courses ("long quizartinib") or no further treatment ("short quizartinib"). Median follow-up was 76 months. Three hundred fourteen patients were FLT3-wild-type (WT); 116 had FLT3 mutations. The primary end point, overall survival (OS) unselected by FLT3 status, showed no significant benefit, and there was a significant increase in non-relapse mortality with quizartinib. In a pre-planned subgroup analysis, patients with FLT3 mutations who received quizartinib had significantly improved OS (Hazard Ratio, 0.59; 95% Confidence Interval, 0.37-0.93; P = .024) due to reduced relapse risk, with greater benefit in the short quizartinib group. In patients with FLT3-WT, there was no survival benefit and no reduction in relapse risk. No significant differences were observed in time to hematologic count recovery or in length of hospitalization. The most observed grade 3/4 adverse events were febrile neutropenia. In conclusion, the addition of quizartinib to intensive chemotherapy, delayed until chemotherapy course 2, prolonged OS in older patients with FLT3-mutated AML but did not improve OS in non-FLT3-selected patients. This trial was registered at www.isrctn.com as ISRCTN-31682779 and at www.clinicaltrialsregister.eu as EudraCR-2013-002730-21.

items.title: Prevalence of Silent Atherosclerosis across Adult Life.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis may begin in early adulthood and remain clinically silent for decades before cardiovascular disease manifests. Although silent atherosclerosis is associated with cardiovascular events and death independent of traditional cardiovascular disease risk factors, its age- and sex-specific prevalence, vascular territory distribution, and plaque volume across adult life remain incompletely defined.
METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study in Denmark and Spain. Adults 18 to 70 years of age without known atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled in five prespecified age strata that included balanced numbers of women and men. Silent atherosclerosis was assessed at baseline with three-dimensional vascular ultrasonography of the carotid and femoral arteries and with coronary computed tomographic angiography.
RESULTS: A total of 16,808 adults were enrolled in the study. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 45±12 years, and 51.4% were women. Silent atherosclerosis was present in 57.1% of the participants (95% confidence interval, 56.3 to 58.0). In the youngest age stratum (18 to 29 years), atherosclerosis was present in 8.7% of the men and 6.7% of the women; prevalence increased with age, with a later, steeper midlife rise among women. Among participants in the younger age strata, atherosclerosis was most often peripheral and confined to a single vascular territory; with increasing age, plaque volume increased exponentially and the prevalence of multiarterial involvement became more frequent. Isolated coronary-artery atherosclerosis was uncommon in every age stratum (≤9.3% of men and ≤5.0% of women).
CONCLUSIONS: This study of silent atherosclerosis showed that the disease was detectable in early adulthood, with age- and sex-associated increases in prevalence across arterial territories and marked increases in plaque volume. items.title: Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting.
items.abstract: Ribosomal frameshifting, an uncommon translational recoding event, is best known for its regulatory roles in viral gene expression1,2, whereas its physiological relevance in mammals remains poorly understood. Here we show that specific codon pairs trigger efficient -1 frameshifting preferentially in cancer cells. Mechanistically, this recoding arises from ribosomal pausing associated with tRNA and amino acid availability, and is amplified by impaired ribosome quality control and sustained phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6. We found that this codon-pair-specific frameshifting represents an intrinsic state of translational dysregulation, which is prevalent across cancer cells and reshapes protein synthesis. Taking advantage of this frameshifting-permissive state in cancer cells, we engineered a frameshifting-activated synthetic therapeutic circuit (FAST) that conditionally expresses the pyroptotic effector gasdermin D. FAST is activated across diverse cancer cell types, inducing potent and selective pyroptosis, while sparing normal tissues from detectable toxicity. As a proof of concept, systemic AAV9-mediated delivery of FAST in mouse models of colorectal and pancreatic cancer elicited pronounced tumour regression, robust immune activation and synergistic effects with immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, these findings reveal codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting as a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells and establish translation-coupled gene circuits as a strategy for cancer-selective therapy.
